findings.suggested_investigation: Check whether TestHarness.h exists in the real worktree outside this snapshot (for example under the shared-source directory that the repo rules name, ../_shared_src, or under tests/include). Check whether stub/_shared is a tracked symlink or ignored/untracked directory. Then run `python3 tools/parity/scenarios.py` from research/companion_levelup and confirm the build line finds TestHarness.h without errors; confirm kt::Report and kt::Check exist and that kt::Report returns nonzero on any failure.
findings.why_it_matters: If TestHarness.h is not shipped with the snapshot or under the include dir the build passes, every harness-based test fails to compile. The gate then stops with COMPILE FAILED rather than passing silently, so this is a build break, not a weakened gate. It is still a portability and reproducibility problem: the header the new harness depends on is not resolvable from the tree that the build flags point at.
